Subject: New model onboarding request + temporary pin (MedPrompt-XL-7B-v2)

Evelyn,

Thanks again for the quick chat this morning. Quixote is ready to start production trials next month and we need Redwood to onboard MedPrompt-XL-7B-v2 as a dedicated serving variant. A few constraints from our side:

- Regulatory: we must be able to demonstrate model lineage and block silent auto-updates for 30 days after initial rollout.
- Performance: target p50 latency <= 140ms at our expected 75% token distribution.
- Safety: we need a model card and the HIPAA questionnaire completed before we go live.

Can you confirm a temporary version pin for the new variant for a 30-day window, with telemetry hooks enabled (prefix telemetry + prompt set evaluation)? Attached: model card, HIPAA questionnaire, a small eval set.

High level timeline we want: onboard in staging by 2028-06-08, canary traffic week of 2028-06-15, production after validation and legal sign-off.

Sanjay
Director of Data Science, Quixote Health

Subject: Re: Fwd: New model onboarding request + temporary pin (MedPrompt-XL-7B-v2)

Quick tech readout after a first pass on the artifacts Quixote shared:

Findings:
- Tokenizer: model uses a custom BPE with a nonstandard merge file; we can load it but will need a small helper to map our canonical tokenizer registry to theirs (no blocking issue).
- KV cache layout: standard causal layout, but attention key dtype is fp16; this is fine for our runtime but we should validate kv restoration path for resharded requests.
- Quantization: they supplied a float32 checkpoint and allow us to apply q4f/ q8x profiles. Recommend we run the initial staging on q8x to match latency targets but keep a float32 fallback for canary failover.

Risks / asks:
1) We need a sample 10k prompt set to simulate prefix caching behavior — the eval bundle they sent has ~500 samples; please ask for the expanded set.
2) Telemetry: we'll enable prefix telemetry and token-level traces but will need explicit consent in contract for sharing aggregated failure metrics back to Quixote.
3) Pin scope: propose a two-stage pin instead of a single 30-day lock:
   - Stage A (provisional): Temporary pin in staging + canary routing for 14 days. Engineering will monitor latency, error-rate, and hallucination regression on the prompt set.
   - Stage B (prod provisional): If Stage A passes, enable a 30-day production pin during which auto-upgrades are disabled; automatic fallback to a vetted model variant will remain available.

Operational plan (high level):
- Day 0: Ingest model, run tokenizer sanity, deploy on staging with q8x.
- Day 3-7: Run synthetic and prefix workloads (we need the 10k set).
- Day 8-14: Canary at 5-10% prod traffic (if performance checks pass).
- Stage B begins after legal sign-off and canary green.

Can you confirm if Quixote can provide the expanded eval bundle and sign the consent for aggregated metrics? Also, Vivek — do we need explicit policy approval for a 30-day production pin for a non-enterprise account?

-Karthik
Lead Integration Engineer

Thanks for the assessment. I'm comfortable approving the two-stage approach Karthik outlined with these guardrails:

- Stage A (staging + canary): up to 14 days as proposed. If engineering flags an unresolved safety or perf regression, lock the model out of production.
- Stage B (production provisional pin): 30 days maximum. Require weekly telemetry summaries to product and Quixote. Legal to confirm the aggregated metrics consent.

Evelyn — please capture the exception in the variant exceptions tracker and add me as approver on the DocuSign envelope. Karthik — proceed with the ingestion plan once we have the 10k prompt bundle and your team confirms q8x staging runs within the latency envelope.

Vivek Kulkarni
VP Product, Redwood Inference
